features.claim: Parasaurolophus had a long, distinctive head crest.
features.quote: Parasaurolophus was a duck-billed dinosaur with a long, distinctive head crest.

features.claim: The crest was a long curved tube that went upwards and back from the skull.
features.quote: They had a large head crest, which was a long curved tube. It went upwards and back from the skull.

features.claim: Parasaurolophus could walk on either two legs or four.
features.quote: Like other hadrosaurids, it was able to walk on either two legs or four.

features.claim: It probably spent most of its life walking on all fours, but could raise itself onto its back legs.
features.quote: It probably spent most of its life walking on all fours, but it could raise itself onto its back legs.
Fossilised skin impressions show that Parasaurolophus had scaly, pebbled skin.

features.claim: It had a beak and toothed jaws.
The crest of a juvenile was low and hemispherical, not long and tubular like the adults.
features.quote: The crest of the juvenile is not long and tubular like the adults, but low and hemispherical.

features.claim: The skull of the P. walkeri type specimen is about 1.6 metres long, including the crest.
features.quote: The skull of the P. walkeri type specimen is about 1.6 metres (5.2 ft) long, including the crest.

debated.claim: Experts have gone back and forth on whether Parasaurolophus walked on two legs or four.
debated.quote: Over the years, experts have gone back and forth as to whether Parasaurolophus walked on two legs or four.

second_reading.claim: The crest was hollow, with a tube running from the nostrils through the crest, looping at the end and going back to the skull.
second_reading.quote: Parasaurolophus is famous for its crest, which was hollow. Starting from the dinosaur's nostrils, an empty tube ran through the crest, looped around at the end and then travelled back to the skull.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: It had hundreds of teeth packed together, but only used a few at a time.
second_reading.quote: Like other members of the hadrosaur group, Parasaurolophus had a complicated arrangement of hundreds of teeth. But it only used a few at a time.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: The idea that the crest was a snorkel is wrong.
second_reading.quote: Most of these hypotheses have been discredited or rejected. For example, there is no hole at the end of the crest for a snorkeling function.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: The idea that the crest held a mobile proboscis is wrong.
second_reading.quote: There are no muscle scars for a proboscis and it is dubious that an animal with a beak would need one.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: The idea that the crest was an air reservoir for staying underwater is wrong.
second_reading.quote: The proposed air reservoir would have been insufficient for an animal the size of Parasaurolophus.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: The idea that the crest was an airlock to keep water out of the lungs is wrong.
second_reading.quote: As a proposed airlock, it would not have kept out water.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Scientists do not know for sure what the crest was for.
second_reading.quote: Nobody knows for sure what the crest was for.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: It is not clear which function of the crest was most significant at what times.
second_reading.quote: It is not clear which was most significant at what times in the evolution of the crest and its internal nasal passages.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it

second_reading.claim: Whether P. cyrtocristatus was a female or a juvenile form is not settled.
second_reading.quote: James Hopson, one of the first researchers to describe lambeosaurine crests in terms of such distinctions, suggested that P. cyrtocristatus, with its small crest, was the female form of P. tubicen. Thomas Williamson suggested it was the juvenile form. Neither hypothesis became widely accepted.
second_reading.why: a picture could not show it
